title: AlphaFold-Multimer virtual screen finds nanobodies that bind and block the itch receptor MRGPRX2
summary: Harvard and UCSF researchers co-folded 10,000 nanobodies with MRGPRX2 in AlphaFold-Multimer; of ten tested, three bound at 20 to 200 nM and blocked mast cell degranulation.
account: Researchers at Harvard Medical School, the University of California, San Francisco and partner institutions used AlphaFold-Multimer to co-fold 10,000 nanobody sequences from a synthetic library design with MRGPRX2, a receptor on mast cells that drives pseudoallergic inflammation and itch. They ranked the pairs by a confidence metric that they had first checked on known nanobody and receptor structures. They expressed and purified ten top-ranked nanobodies. Three (Sim8619, Sim9877 and Sim4784) bound MRGPRX2 with affinities between about 20 and 200 nM and blocked mast cell degranulation caused by Compound 48/80; mutations supported the predicted binding pose. Nature Communications published the study on 23 April 2026. The work is a laboratory proof of concept for one receptor, and some authors are co-inventors on a patent application for the nanobodies.
purpose: AlphaFold-Multimer was built to predict the structures of protein complexes. The researchers used it to discover binders, an application by an independent group.
system: AlphaFold-Multimer (AF-M), run through a modified ColabFold script
deployer: Harvard Medical School (Kruse laboratory) and University of California, San Francisco (Susa laboratory)
location: Boston, Massachusetts, and San Francisco, California, United States

ratings.reason: A purely computational screen yielded three nanomolar MRGPRX2 antagonists from ten candidates tested.

ai_role.statement: The authors tested only AlphaFold-Multimer picks; they had no arm with randomly chosen or experimentally screened nanobodies.
